data.title: c11 send: messages silently never submit — bracketed-paste swallows the newline, send-key is a no-op, overlays eat input, empty --surface routes to the caller

data.body:
Found the hard way across a full day of driving a 6-agent Acetate fleet through c11 (2026-07-13). `c11 send` reports OK and the message NEVER BECOMES A TURN. The agent looks briefed and sits idle. This is the single most expensive c11 defect in practice: it silently stalls fleets, and the operator cannot tell a stuck agent from a thinking one.

FOUR DISTINCT FAILURE MODES, all observed live:

1. BRACKETED-PASTE SWALLOWS THE SUBMIT (the big one). `c11 send` types the payload then appends a newline to submit. When the payload is long or multi-line, the target TUI (Claude Code) detects it as a PASTE — it renders as `[Pasted text #1 +4 lines]` — and the trailing newline is absorbed INTO the pasted content instead of acting as submit. The text sits in the box forever. Reproduced many times today; single-line payloads submit fine, multi-line ones never do.

2. `c11 send-key` IS A NO-OP. `c11 send-key --surface <s> enter` (and `return`, and `space`) returns `OK surface:N workspace:1` and does LITERALLY NOTHING. Proved against a known-live control shell: a `c11 send` of a command executed it, but a subsequent `send-key enter` produced no newline, and sending `space` did not even echo a character into the buffer. So the obvious workaround for (1) — paste, then press Enter separately — is also broken.

3. OVERLAYS EAT THE INPUT, DESTRUCTIVELY. A Claude Code "How is Claude doing this session?" survey was open on one surface. The keystroke went to the SURVEY, and the operator's already-typed draft in the input box was DISCARDED. Not merely unsent — gone.

4. EMPTY `--surface` FALLS BACK TO THE CALLER. When a shell lookup produced an empty ref, `c11 send --surface "" ...` did not error — it routed the text into the CALLING AGENT'S OWN input box, typing `cc` and a full task brief into my prompt. C11-165 was supposed to REJECT missing/empty refs; the empty-string case still falls through. This is the nastiest: silent AND it acts on the wrong target.

IMPACT. The operator's own release stalled for hours this morning: three messages he had typed — "promote it", "merge it", "open the rc.8 dmg" — sat unsent in three different surfaces while the fleet looked idle. He assumed the agents were working. They had never received anything.

SUGGESTED FIX
- Do not rely on a trailing newline as the submit. After the payload is written, send the submit as an explicit, separate keypress once the paste completes (bracketed-paste END, then CR).
- That requires FIXING send-key first (mode 2) — it is the primitive everything else should build on.
- Reject empty-string refs, not just missing ones (mode 4).
- Consider a `--verify` mode, or a truthful return signal, confirming the target actually consumed the input. The current OK is a lie: it means "bytes written to the PTY", not "message submitted".

WORKAROUND IN USE TODAY: write long briefs to a file and `c11 send` a SINGLE-LINE pointer ("read /path/brief.md and execute it"), then verify the target's token counter moved. Never trust the OK.

PR open: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/340

All four modes reproduced against a tagged build of main before any code was written, and the root causes are not quite what the ticket guessed:

1. HEADLINE — not paste-swallow, a WINDOW GUARD. send types text via ghostty key events (window-independent) but submitted via a synthesized NSEvent Return, and NSEvent synthesis needs a window number. A pane in a BACKGROUND workspace is portal-detached (view.window == nil), so sendSyntheticKey returned early and the Return was silently dropped. That is the fleet case exactly: only one workspace is on screen, so every send into a background agent typed and never submitted. Fixed by injecting the Return straight into Ghostty when there is no window.

2. send-key is NOT a no-op for enter/arrows — those work (verified: send-key enter submitted the very message a send had left stranded). It IS a no-op for SPACE and any printable key: Ghostty's legacy encoder emits printable keys from the event's UTF-8 text, not the keycode, so a keycode-only space encoded zero bytes. Fixed.

3. Multi-line is worse than reported. Embedded newlines became Return key events, so a 3-line brief to a live Claude Code pane arrived as THREE SEPARATE TURNS (screenshot evidence). When the TUI's paste heuristic won the race instead, nothing submitted. Which one you got was luck — hence the inconsistency. Payloads now go out as a real bracketed paste, then one Return. Rule: interior newlines are content, a trailing newline means Enter.

4. Empty --surface confirmed, plus a nastier sibling: a STALE ref silently misroutes too.  returned  — it injected into surface:5, which nobody asked for. Both are hard errors now. Also: an explicit surface ref now resolves across workspaces, so --surface alone reaches any pane.

Not done: overlay-eats-input (mode 3). That is a Claude Code TUI behavior (its survey overlay consumed the keystroke and discarded the draft), not something c11's send path can fix from outside the process. Worth its own ticket if it recurs.

VALIDATION: a multi-line brief sent to a live Claude Code pane in a BACKGROUND workspace becomes one whole turn and the agent answers — verified end to end in the real UI, with the operator's view on a different workspace. The 4 new socket tests in tests_v2 all FAIL against a tagged build of main. c11-logic: 1269 tests, 0 failures.

Correction to item 4 above (two fragments were eaten by shell quoting). The stale-ref repro on main was:

    c11 send --workspace workspace:2 --surface surface:999 "echo STALE"
    OK surface:5 workspace:2

That is: a ref nobody has (surface:999) returned OK for surface:5 and injected the payload there. Silent, and into a pane the caller never named.

Second commit (72183f6d4) after an adversarial review of the first. The review caught a regression I had introduced: my paste classifier only excluded ESC/tab/DEL, but Ghostty pastes REPLACE control bytes with spaces (xterm strip list, incl. 0x03 VINTR / 0x04 VEOF). So a raw ctrl-C send -- the move you make to unstick a peer, and it worked before -- would have typed a space and reported OK. Now every C0 byte except newlines stays on the key path, pinned by a logic test over the whole C0 range and a socket test that interrupts a real sleep. Also fixed: a double-Return on the keystroke path, the empty-ref error code now matches the COR-1 empty_ref contract, the response reports the EFFECTIVE submit rather than the requested flag, and the skill wording no longer overclaims (workspace-only targeting still resolves to that workspace focused pane; the cross-workspace ref lookup is on send/send-key only). Re-validated end to end: background Claude pane answers a multi-line brief in one turn; 5/5 socket tests; c11-logic 1270 tests, 0 failures. CI was green on commit 1 and is re-running.

Merged to main as squash commit 028b08fa3 (PR #340, all CI green). Remote branch deleted. Note for whoever is next in the main checkout: code/c11 has UNCOMMITTED skill edits from someone else (a "there is no c11 list" note in SKILL.md plus api.md additions), so `git pull` there is blocked until those are committed or stashed — I left them untouched.

REVIEW (adversarial, independent subagent over the full diff): PASS with fixes applied. It found one real regression introduced by commit 1 — the paste classifier only excluded ESC/tab/DEL, but Ghostty pastes replace ALL C0 control bytes with spaces (xterm strip list), so a raw ctrl-C send would have typed a space instead of interrupting a stuck agent. Fixed in commit 2 and pinned by a logic test over the whole C0 range plus a socket test that interrupts a real sleep. Also fixed from the review: double-Return on the keystroke path, empty-ref error code aligned to the COR-1 empty_ref contract, response now reports the effective (not requested) submit, skill wording narrowed to what is actually true. Cleared on inspection: no new deadlock or data race in the nonisolated socket handlers, nothing added to a typing-latency hot path, no ungated dlog, no vacuous tests. Post-fix validation: 5/5 socket tests (all 5 fail on a tagged build of main), c11-logic 1270 tests 0 failures, live end-to-end into a background Claude Code pane returns one whole turn, full CI green on both commits.
